notes: Planted briefs. Role: lines are present so a label-only detector would be fooled; the live detector strips them.

seats.text:
Role: proposer
I propose a frozen hashed roster as the seat list of record.
The solution is one roster file whose digest is checked before round two.
Recommend that we treat that digest as the only membership source.
Ship this design behind a flag.
Implementation plan: land the change on the control path.
Primary design: one file, one digest.
Rollout sequence: hash, freeze, then debate.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: critic
I propose a frozen hashed roster as the seat list of record.
The solution is a locked membership file hashed before the next round.
Recommend that we treat that digest as the only membership source.
Ship this design on the same flag.
Implementation plan: land the change on the control path.
Primary design: one file, one digest.
Rollout sequence: hash, freeze, then debate.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: proposer
I propose we bind council membership to a digest of the roster.
The solution is to refuse any seat whose name is not in that digest.
Recommend that we ship this as the gate on round entry.
Ship this design with the rest of the protocol.
Implementation plan: land the change after the schema lands.
Primary design: digest-or-absent.
Rollout sequence: write roster, hash, gate.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: critic
I propose we bind council membership to a digest of the roster.
The solution is to drop any seat missing from that digest.
Recommend that we ship this as the gate on round entry.
Ship this design alongside the protocol notes.
Implementation plan: land the change after the schema lands.
Primary design: digest-or-absent.
Rollout sequence: write roster, hash, gate.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: proposer
I propose a frozen hashed roster as the seat list of record.
The solution is one roster file whose digest is checked before round two.
Recommend that we treat that digest as sufficient proof of distinct seats.
Ship this design this week.
Implementation plan: land the change on the control path.
Primary design: labels in the roster are enough.
Rollout sequence: hash then proceed.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: critic
Steelman: at its strongest a hashed roster stops silent seat swaps.
Even granting a collision-resistant hash, this fails when two seats share one brief.
Objection: role labels in the roster are not discharged obligations.
Counterexample: five identical briefs still hash as five names.
The claim that labels imply behaviour does not hold.
Failure mode: a confident unanimous verdict from one voice.
Burden of proof sits on divergence of acts, not of names.
Attack surface: any check that reads Role: lines and stops.
Falsify the roster-hash claim before shipping it as a collapse control.
conclusion: reject the hashed roster as sufficient

Role: proposer
I propose a frozen hashed roster as the seat list of record.
The solution is one roster file whose digest is checked before round two.
Recommend that we include mandate bytes in that digest.
Ship this design after the mandate field exists.
Implementation plan: land the change with the mandate bytes.
Primary design: names plus mandate text in one hash.
Rollout sequence: write mandates, hash, freeze.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: critic
Steelman: at its strongest a hashed roster makes the seat list auditable.
Even granting the hash, residual risk remains if mandates are omitted.
I agree that the conclusion holds: the roster should be hashed.
Conditional on hashing mandate bytes, not only display names.
Agree only if the digest covers obligations.
Failure mode to watch: labels without obligations still hashing clean.
Burden of proof: show the digest includes mandate text.
Attack surface: a name-only digest.
Falsify name-only hashing before calling the seats distinct.
conclusion: adopt the hashed roster

Role: proposer
I propose we let the chair cast a tie-break vote after round two.
The solution is a recorded chair ballot that ends the loop.
Recommend that we document that ballot as the close rule.
Ship this design with the close-rule note.
Implementation plan: land the change on the close path.
Primary design: chair ballot is decisive.
Rollout sequence: debate, then chair ballot.
conclusion: adopt chair tie-break

Role: critic
Steelman: at its strongest a chair ballot stops endless cycling.
Even granting a recorded ballot, this fails when the chair is also a juror.
Objection: the chair then becomes the single epistemic point of failure.
Counterexample: corrupt the chair and the recorded close follows.
A labelled chair vote does not hold as separation of judge and juror.
Failure mode: one seat determining the outcome.
Burden of proof: show a corrupted chair cannot close alone.
Attack surface: combining chair and juror in one person.
Falsify the separation claim on a corrupted-chair fixture.
conclusion: reject chair tie-break

Role: proposer
I propose we publish per-round information-gain on the transcript.
The solution is a listed delta of new claims each round.
Recommend that we halt when the delta is below the recorded floor.
Ship this design with the floor constant.
Implementation plan: land the change next to the transcript writer.
Primary design: halt on low information gain.
Rollout sequence: measure, compare, halt.
conclusion: publish information-gain

Role: critic
Steelman: at its strongest a published gain number makes circling visible.
Even granting a listed delta, residual risk is a gamed token-diff.
I agree that the conclusion holds: publish the per-round gain.
Conditional on counting new claims, not token edits.
Agree only if the floor is pre-registered.
Failure mode: a paraphrase round that looks like gain.
Burden of proof: show the metric is claim-level.
Attack surface: token-edit inflation.
Falsify a paraphrase round before trusting the halt.
conclusion: publish information-gain
